ambiguities.clauseRef: 90% of net after expenses. Expenses capped $3050.
ambiguities.description: When actual expenses exceed the $3,050 cap, it is unclear whether 'net' is calculated using actual expenses or the capped amount. If capped, the artist benefits when actuals exceed the cap; if actual, the venue absorbs nothing above the cap and the artist bears the overage.

plausibleReadings.summary: Net is calculated using only the capped $3,050, regardless of actual expenses — overage stays with the venue
plausibleReadings.impact: Artist-favorable when actuals exceed cap. On a $5,000 gross with $4,000 actual expenses, artist gets 90% of $1,950 ($1,755) vs. 90% of $1,000 ($900) — a $855 difference.

plausibleReadings.summary: Net is calculated using actual expenses up to the cap, and the cap is simply a ceiling the venue agrees not to exceed — both parties share the assumption actuals won't go over
plausibleReadings.impact: Neutral if actuals stay under $3,050; becomes venue-favorable if actuals are allowed to creep above the stated cap through a loose interpretation of what's included.

ambiguities.suggestedClarification: To confirm: if actual expenses exceed $3,050, is net calculated using the capped $3,050 (artist gets the upside) or using actual expenses (venue absorbs the overage some other way)? And does the cap include all venue operating costs, or only specific categories?

sourceText: 90% of net after expenses. Expenses capped $3050. No guarantee.
